newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty firms again, depos up on dry market.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty firms again, depos up on dry market.

text.p: The Polish zloty strengthened to a new six month high at more than 2.7 percent from the trading band centre on Wednesday after a week-long currency-selling trend continued this morning, dealers said.
They said the currency-selling sentiment was not as strong as in past days, but large enough to set a new peak for the zloty, the highest from late May's three percent from parity.
Dealers said that the sentiment faded by mid-morning and left the zloty drifting in line with dollar/mark swings.
"After some early currency selling the zloty was left to track dollar/mark," said Marcin Turkiewicz of Bank Zachodni SA.
The zloty closed at 2.74/2.71 percent from the trading band centre, stronger than Tuesday's close at 2.67/2.63 percent.
It closed at 2.8632/40 to the dollar, down from 2.8625/33 on Tuesday and at 1.8341/47 marks, down from 1.8300/10.

Some dealers said the cental bank would not intervenue on the forex market to stop the zloty's gains, as it had done earlier this year, as long as currency inflows resulted from privatisation or capital increases of foreign banks in Poland.
"As long as the inflow of currencies is structural and not speculative the central bank is likely to refrain from interventions," one dealer at a Polish bank said.
The National Bank of Poland (NBP) last intervened on the forex market on May 22 when the NBP bought dollars at about three percent from the average dollar and mark parity rates.

The money market remained tight with most players searching for cash, which kept one-day deposit bids at a high level of 23 percent and dealers said the shortage may continue in upcoming days as there were no large inflows later this week.
"Big banks sought funds even for longer periods. This might be the market's response to the NBP's recent statement that market rates may rise," said Elzbieta Adamska from BIG SA.
The NBP had signalled last month that market rates may rise in upcoming months to cap excessive growth of credit action.
Overnight rates were at 23.00/24.50 percent against the opening at 23.00/24.00 percent. Tomorrow/next rates were at 23.40/24.30 percent against 23.50/24.20 pct at 0950 GMT.
The NBP had not staged an open market opertation since November 28.
